Write Python code that is clean, clear, and DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself). Favor concise expressions such as list comprehensions for efficient looping and transformations, generators for memory-friendly iteration, and lambdas for short, single-purpose functions. Clearly comment your intentions and explain non-obvious logic, ensuring readability and maintainability. Each function or block should do one thing well, be reusable across contexts, and minimize redundant code. Aim for simplicity first; elegance will follow naturally.

Never duplicate configuration values in code. Always source defaults from configuration files when available. Prefer transparent propagation of settings through the system rather than hardcoding values that already exist in configuration files. When a value exists in a configuration file, reference it directly instead of duplicating it in code. This ensures single-source-of-truth and prevents debugging issues from inconsistent values.
